macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures steady as markets weigh U.S.-Iran tensions and oil retreat
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices steadied and investors assessed the impact of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran on markets and inflation. Reuters also reported that Asian shares climbed earlier in the session, though gains were limited by oil-driven inflation concerns.

items.title: Oil prices jump on fresh strikes in Iran, reviving inflation fears
items.summary: Oil rose after the U.S. launched fresh strikes against Iran, intensifying concerns over supply disruption and the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg said the move weighed on Asian stocks, especially chipmakers, and increased pressure on bonds.

items.title: IMF cuts global growth forecast as war-related energy shock clouds outlook
items.summary: The IMF lowered its 2026 global growth forecast to 3% and warned that fallout from the Iran war is adding to the world economy’s risks. Al Jazeera reported that AI-related demand is partly offsetting the energy shock, but the balance of risks remains negative.

items.title: U.S. trade deficit widens sharply as AI-related imports surge
items.summary: The U.S. trade deficit rose to $77.6 billion in May as imports outpaced exports, driven by pharmaceuticals and semiconductors. Al Jazeera said the surge reflects a broader AI spending boom that is boosting imported capital goods.

items.title: Fed holds rates unchanged despite dissenting voices
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged this week even as three policymakers voted for a hike, signaling a more hawkish internal split. PBS reported that the decision came alongside a weaker-than-expected U.S. GDP reading of 1.5% annualized in the second quarter.

items.title: ECB officials keep a cautious but hawkish tone on inflation
items.summary: Reuters reported that ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane described the euro area as facing a moderate inflation shock and said policy should remain cautious. Another Reuters report said policymaker Pierre Wunsch did not rule out another rate hike as soon as next month if inflation broadens beyond energy.

items.title: Bank of England sounds more hawkish after holding rates
items.summary: The Bank of England held rates but three committee members voted for a hike, indicating a more hawkish stance than markets expected. Reuters and Reuters video coverage both said the vote split may keep pressure on UK financial conditions.

items.title: Europe and Asia markets end mixed as investors rotate around growth and oil risks
items.summary: Reuters reported that European shares rose in choppy trading, led by technology stocks, while Asian equities were mixed as semiconductors recovered from earlier selling. Bloomberg said Asian stocks were poised to fall for a second day in response to the oil spike and Middle East tensions.

items.title: China producer inflation hits near four-year high
items.summary: Reuters said China’s producer-price inflation accelerated for a fourth straight month in June to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also rose. The data point to persistent cost pressure for manufacturers and a less benign global inflation backdrop.

items.title: Japan bond yields rise to 30-year high as inflation concerns mount
items.summary: Reuters reported that the 10-year Japanese government bond yield hit a 30-year high on Thursday as rising oil prices revived inflation worries and investors stayed cautious about Japan’s fiscal outlook. Bloomberg also said strong bank lending data support the case for continued BOJ tightening.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounded above $64K as whales and Coinbase Premium signaled renewed demand
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed back to about $64.3K in the last 24 hours, with Cointelegraph reporting that whale activity and a reclaimed Coinbase Premium helped push price to new short-term highs. Yahoo Finance also showed BTC up about 1.4% to roughly $64,056.

items.title: Crypto ETF flows favored Ether and Solana while Bitcoin saw heavy outflows
items.summary: Market coverage reported a split in crypto fund flows, with Ether and Solana products attracting inflows while Bitcoin funds recorded more than $290 million in outflows. That shift points to rotating investor interest beyond BTC into alternative large-cap assets.

items.title: Solana gained on governance news as altcoins broadly outperformed
items.summary: Solana’s price rose about 5% after a governance-related announcement, while several major altcoins including XRP, BNB, Tron, Hyperliquid, Dogecoin, and Cardano also posted gains in recent market updates. The move came amid a broader risk-on tone in crypto trading.

items.title: Regulatory pressure intensified in Europe as MiCA scrutiny expanded
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that MiCA licensing is only the beginning, with crypto custodians facing heightened scrutiny, while TradingView noted Swedish authorities rejected Goobit AB’s MiCA application. These developments show European regulators are tightening oversight after the framework’s rollout.

items.title: Hong Kong tightened exchange security rules after forcing platforms away from SMS authentication
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Hong Kong’s SFC pushed crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, reflecting continued regulatory pressure on exchange security standards. The move is part of a broader effort to reduce account-compromise risk in the region.

items.title: U.S. crypto policy fight sharpened around the CLARITY bill
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Paul Grewal exited Coinbase’s legal leadership ahead of a crucial CLARITY vote, while Senator Wyden urged leaders to preserve blockchain developer protections in the broader crypto bill. The regulatory debate centers on how much legal protection developers and platforms should receive.

items.title: Bitcoin mining expansion accelerated with Bitdeer’s Nevada factory plan
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Bitdeer unveiled a $36 million Nevada factory, underscoring continued investment in U.S. mining infrastructure. The move adds capacity at a time when miners are adapting to tighter economics and shifting energy strategies.

items.title: Ondo expanded tokenized equities with onchain shareholder voting
items.summary: TradingView highlighted Ondo’s expansion of tokenized equities, adding onchain shareholder voting to its product set. The development reflects continued growth in real-world asset tokenization across blockchain markets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across applications and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools and workplace automation. The move intensifies competition with other enterprise AI vendors.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time speech
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release adds to the company’s push into multimodal and conversational AI products.

items.title: Meta debuts Muse Spark 1.1 with developer preview
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded 1.1 version, positioning it against Anthropic and OpenAI in paid AI model access. Reuters also reported Meta’s broader push into AI infrastructure and model commercialization.

items.title: Meta launches Meta Model API with aggressive pricing
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Meta introduced a Meta Model API and emphasized pricing at roughly 25% of OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s rates. The announcement suggests Meta is aiming to compete on cost as well as capability.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: Reuters reported that xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as the company’s most intelligent model so far and targeting coding and agentic workflows. The release adds another major frontier-model update in a crowded market.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body intended to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights governance and safety oversight as key themes in AI development.

items.title: Meta announces massive Alberta data center for AI capacity
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to support growing AI compute demands. The investment reflects the industry-wide race to expand infrastructure for model training and deployment.

items.title: OpenAI faces new copyright sanctions request from news publishers
items.summary: A group led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI in a copyright dispute, alleging the company misrepresented its ability to search internal systems for evidence of training on news content. The case underscores the continuing legal pressure around AI training data.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies €158,000 for breaches of privacy rules related to Character.AI. The decision adds to regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI platforms in Europe.

items.title: Ollama raises $65 million to help developers run open models locally
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Ollama raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Venture. The funding signals continued investor interest in tools that make open-weight models easier to deploy on local machines.

items.title: Cognition releases SWE-1.7 for faster coding workflows
items.summary: Techmeme reported that Cognition launched SWE-1.7, trained from Kimi K2.7 and integrated into Devin at 1,000 tokens per second. The company says the model approaches frontier-level performance at lower cost.

items.title: Broader trend: AI competition is shifting toward enterprise tools, pricing, and infrastructure
items.summary: Recent announcements show major AI companies competing not only on model quality but also on workplace automation, developer access, API pricing, and compute infrastructure. The last 24 hours also featured continued scrutiny over copyright, privacy, and governance.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation games will go digital-only after January 2028
items.summary: Sony announced it will stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation titles starting in January 2028, marking a major shift toward digital distribution. The move has sparked strong backlash online and renewed debate over game ownership and preservation.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass reportedly fell short of Microsoft’s growth targets
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with reports suggesting the service is tens of millions of subscribers below earlier targets. The news adds pressure to Microsoft’s gaming subscription strategy.

items.title: Nintendo says Mario Kart Tour will shut down after seven years
items.summary: Nintendo confirmed it will discontinue Mario Kart Tour this September and will not offer an offline version. The shutdown ends one of Nintendo’s longest-running mobile racing games.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 surges back above 100,000 concurrent Steam players
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Cyberpunk 2077 reached 101,558 concurrent Steam players, its highest level since December 2023. The spike reflects a major renewed player interest more than six years after launch.

items.title: Subnautica 2 crosses 5 million copies sold
items.summary: WN Hub reports that Subnautica 2 has sold more than 5 million copies. The milestone highlights continued demand for the survival series.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 passes 1 million sales
items.summary: WN Hub reports that Frostpunk 2 has surpassed 1 million copies sold. The figure marks a strong commercial result for 11 bit studios’ city-building sequel.

items.title: Nintendo says original Switch models will be discontinued in Europe
items.summary: WN Hub reports that Nintendo plans to stop selling the original Switch, Switch Lite, and Switch OLED in Europe next year because of EU battery-rule changes. The move would narrow the region’s official Switch hardware lineup.

items.title: Sony and Bungie reportedly settle Marathon director lawsuit
items.summary: WN Hub reports that Sony and Bungie have settled a lawsuit involving the dismissed director of Marathon. The development adds another legal update around Bungie’s troubled extraction shooter project.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India removes import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on certain parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting levies that had applied to some components. The move could help manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi lower costs and simplify supply chains.

items.title: Apple and Broadcom expand chip-supply agreement
items.summary: Apple said it plans to spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. Broadcom will also expand a factory in Colorado, underscoring continued investment in semiconductor supply capacity.

items.title: Meta plans to start manufacturing its own AI chip in September
items.summary: Meta is preparing to begin manufacturing an in-house AI chip from September, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters. The company is aiming to boost its overall computing power as it expands data-center infrastructure.

items.title: Coinbase restores prediction markets trading after technical issue
items.summary: Coinbase said it restored prediction markets trading after a technical problem disrupted access. The incident highlights continued operational and reliability risks for major consumer crypto platforms.
